packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-07 - unverified blind image reading (reader D)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this fragment was in my
  context.
- Beyond the brief: I made contrast-boosted 2x enlargements of tiles 002,
  003, 005, 006 in my scratchpad folder (readerD/) to read them. No other
  files opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001: face A (labelled "A" card), one narrow parchment strip c. 4.5 x
  14.5 cm, cut into three tongues top and bottom (binding stub / guard).
  A pencil number "9?6" / "976?" (modern) is written vertically in the left
  margin. Left margin blank with a vertical ruled line; text column to the
  right, ruled in red/pink ink, c. 32 written lines visible, brown-black
  ink, small gothic book hand with heavy abbreviation. The right side of
  the column is lost (irregular tear), so every line is truncated at the
  right, more so in the lower half.
- image-004: the other face (also labelled A). Mirror layout: text on the
  left, torn at the left edge, blank margin with ruled line at right. So the
  lines of this face are truncated at their BEGINNINGS. Same hand, c. 31-32
  lines.
- Tiles: 002 (face 1 upper), 003 (face 1 lower; first 4 lines overlap 002's
  last 4), 005 (face 2 upper), 006 (face 2 lower; first 4 lines overlap 005's
  last 4). Overlap treated once.
- Proper names in the text are written with capitals (Martha, Maria,
  Lucas?, Jacob?) and there are paragraph-like capitals at line starts
  (S-, Q-, M-). No rubrics or coloured initials visible; red is only ruling.
- No glosses or marginalia except the modern pencil number.
- Face order (which is recto) cannot be determined from the images.

TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: (x) expansion; x? uncertain; [..] lost or [illegible]; lines
counted from the top of each image. Face 1 lines end at a tear; face 2 lines
begin at a tear.

  l.7   [..]deus? / [..]dens? alius? (?)s? d(e)signat? g(r)a(tia)?
  l.8   [..] . Dicit? (et)? duplex? turris? / tu(r)ris?

  l.10  [..]p(er)auit? q(uo)n(iam)? t(em)p(o)r(e)? p(ri)m(us)? / q(uo)n(iam) p(ri)mus
  l.11  [..] (?)pal? / spual? ad p(er)fectio(n)e(m)? / p(ro)fectu(m)?
  l.12  [..] (?)e? de? xij? / xvi? . rec[..]
  l.13  [..]tas? (?)a p(re)cedit? / p(re)cedda (et) q(uo)d?
  l.14  [..]erat? / [..]reuat? ap(osto)l(u)s? / ap(?)mis? . It(em)? .ri.?
  l.15  [..]lim? (?) e(st)? / (et) mundu(m)? haut? / mundi haue[..]
        [end of written column]

SELECTED / UNREAD
- I transcribed every visible line of both faces. Line beginnings on face 2
  and line ends on face 1 are physically lost. Readings with no "?" are the
  more secure ones: e.g. face 1 "martha", "habuerat", "ad maiore(m)",
  "respondere?", "Quo(modo) putas maria", "Maria itaq(ue)"; face 2
  "o(mn)ia relinq(ue)ndo", "secuti sunt eu(m)", "uenator fuit", "ut
  supplantauit", "q(uo)d ille p(er)dit (per) sup(er)bia(m)", "magni
  (con)silij", "regno celor(um)", "duo bra[..]", "ad p(er)fectio(n)e(m)?".
- Uncertain throughout: the many abbreviation-heavy words (marked ?).

LIMITATIONS
- Tile resolution is modest (c. 700 px wide); higher-resolution capture would
  settle many letter-level doubts (minims, c/t, s/f, abbreviation marks).
- Fold creases run vertically through the middle of the column on both
  faces and obscure 1-2 letters per line.
